sentences.text: [earnest] Can't afford to save more right now? Save from your next raise. In one well-known study, savings went from three and a half percent to thirteen point six.

visual.small: Can't afford to save more right now?

sentences.text: Otherwise every raise quietly turns into lifestyle. Here's what to flip.
Workers at one company agreed, in advance, to put part of each future raise into savings.

visual.source: Thaler & Benartzi, Journal of Political Economy, 2004

sentences.text: Over about forty months, their savings rate went from three point five to thirteen point six percent.
One company, so it's one study, not a promise.

visual.title: Savings rate of those who joined
visual.source: One employer's plan. A DOL review rates the causal evidence low.

sentences.text: So turn on auto-increase in your 401(k).
Or set a rule: half of every raise goes to savings the week it lands.

pairs.right: Half of every raise to savings

sentences.text: [warm] Send this to whoever has a review soon. Before it lands.
